sections.h2: Mineral fuels alone import more than the whole $189 billion target

chart.title: Fuels and precious stones and gold are 40.3 per cent of imports
chart.sub: Imports by chapter, FY2025-26, $ million. Top five chapters.
chart.source: DGCI&S TradeStat, FY2025-26 provisional; shares computed in the original.
chart.accent: 1. HS 27 — Mineral Fuels, Mineral Oils And Products Of

sections.means: Mineral fuels and pearls, precious stones and gold together make up 40.3 per cent of imports, and neither can be made in India.
sections.todo: Ask for the denominator: state every substitution target as a share of the import lines it can actually replace.

sections.h2: The $189 billion matches a mid-tail band, not all large import lines

chart.title: The $189 billion fits a mid-tail band, not the $722.3 billion above $50 million
chart.sub: Annual imports by band, $ billion, FY2025-26.
chart.source: DGCI&S 8-digit commodity data, FY2025-26; band totals computed in the original.

sections.means: The reported $189 billion over 1,272 products averages $148.6 million each, close to the $50 million to $500 million band.
sections.todo: Publish the product list with its import value, so the $189 billion can be checked against the band.

sections.h2: Electronics, the largest addressable target, has doubled since FY2018-19

chart.title: Electronics imports rose through the years the PLI schemes were meant to cut them
chart.sub: Electronics (HS 85) import value, $ million, first and latest financial year.
chart.source: DGCI&S; chapter mapping is this article's own.

sections.means: Electronics imports went from $52,049 million in FY2018-19 to $104,853 million in FY2025-26, slightly more than double.
sections.todo: Track electronics imports alongside output, since assembly pulls in imported components and output alone will not show the gap.
